societies.name: Forbidden Planet (Morbius’s robot-supported household)
societies.society: Morbius and Altaira’s continuing robotic-production household

scope.period: The established two-human household before the visiting crew and final destruction
scope.population: Morbius and his living daughter Altaira
exclusions: Extinct Krell counted as current residents
A claim of United Planets-wide post-work rights

societies.description:
Morbius and Altaira have an implemented, continuing support arrangement rather than merely a large fortune. Robby reproduces food chemically and performs material household service, allowing the isolated pair to obtain necessities without earning wages or importing an ordinary workforce. The guarantee estimate is strong inside this two-person unit, while remaining conditional on a private household and its functioning machinery. It is not universal citizenship or proof that the surrounding civilization has ended work.

Morbius designs, programs and commands the producer, so effective productive control is concentrated in one human. Robby’s intelligence and protective limits do not make the robot an independent economic ruler. Human work continues in another form: Morbius studies the Krell, and Altaira’s learning or animal care can also be useful activity. The central participation estimate treats her mainly recreational life as nonworking and Morbius as working, with a range allowing both to count as useful workers. That is a transparent two-person interpretation, not a general labor statistic. The later rescue and destruction of the planet end this particular arrangement.

guarantees.basis: The continuing household has actual synthetic food and robotic service; no wage condition is depicted, but support remains privately controlled and not universally available.

control.basis: Morbius creates and programs Robby and directs its productive activity; safety constraints are not broad resident ownership.

nonworking.basis: For two living residents, Morbius’s sustained research means at least one works. The central estimate treats Altaira as primarily leisured; if her learning or care is sustained useful work, the fraction can be zero. This bounded role scenario is not canonical.

evidence.claim: A continuing isolated household uses actual food replication and robotic service under Morbius’s command.
evidence.locator: AFI household/lunch synopsis; Robby character and synthetic-food dialogue entries

uncertainties: A deliberately tiny household unit with actual production, distinct from a rich protagonist simply buying goods.
The participation estimate has a two-person denominator and cannot represent a whole country or species.
The scientist’s voluntary research and potentially useful care/learning still count as work.
No historical Krell entitlement or post-destruction future is inferred.

review.method: Second pass against the gathered passages, including explicit uncertainty; no independent reviewer

decisions.reason: THX 1138’s human workers perform actual industrial production.
decisions.analysis: Robot police and computer mediation do not establish unnecessary human work or general labor-independent access.

decisions.reason: Metropolis shows an exploited workforce and robot prototype rather than an implemented post-work support system.
decisions.analysis: Potential replacement and robot impersonation are not realized universal automation or deliberate preservation of dispensable jobs.

decisions.reason: Everytown’s 2036 technological prosperity does not settle household distribution or labor independence.
decisions.analysis: The source verifies the film’s year and advanced city, but science, peace and disease control do not supply an economic constitution.
decisions.follow_up: Skip film/novel reconstruction; do not import different chronology or policies from Wells’s book.

decisions.reason: Krell thought-production technology does not establish a durable, generally accessible pre-extinction support arrangement.
decisions.analysis: A technological culmination and catastrophic outcome are not a verified long-lived entitlement system or a justified alien participation denominator.
decisions.follow_up: Skip speculative historical reconstruction; the living human household has its own narrower record.

decisions.reason: The two-human household has actual continuing synthetic-food production and robotic service, with its limited unit disclosed.
Robotic control of aggression does not establish the interplanetary society’s material provision system.
decisions.analysis: Klaatu’s speech concerns enforcement and peace, not ordinary goods, ownership or labor participation. Absolute power in one jurisdiction is not authority over every productive function.

decisions.reason: The 2008 alien intervention is not a depicted civilian post-work society.
decisions.analysis: Planetary destruction, preservation missions and a halted attack do not establish resident production and access. The earlier film’s treaty is a different continuity.

decisions.reason: Colossus establishes coercive control but only promises the material plenty needed for this lead.
decisions.analysis: Nuclear leverage and a future abundance speech do not demonstrate an already functioning labor-independent supply system; novel and film institutions are not combined.

decisions.reason: Delos supplies a purchased temporary leisure service, not a durable supported resident society.
decisions.analysis: Android performance does not make paying tourists independent of outside income, and actual technical staff remain at work.
decisions.follow_up: Keep as a leisure-industry automation comparison.

decisions.reason: Futureworld’s resort and replacement scheme do not establish a post-work civilian support order.
decisions.analysis: Robot doubles and a corporate conspiracy change control risks without establishing distribution of necessities.
decisions.follow_up: Skip speculative extrapolation beyond the realized film plot.

review_notes: Ten reference-led film decisions and one deliberately tiny but materially explicit household record.
Morbius’s actual continuing fabrication qualifies the limited unit; mere personal wealth would not. Its two-person participation scenario stays visible.
Krell extinction does not prohibit historical research, but the short source does not establish a durable pre-extinction entitlement regime.
Things to Come uses the verified film year 2036. Peace-enforcement power, promised abundance and temporary tourism are not universal economic arrangements.
